 JUDGMENT
This petition is filed u/s.166 of M.V. Act 1989 for claiming compensation on account of death of Sri.Bijay Magar S/o Late Yam B. Magar.

2. The brief facts of the case is that, on 13.09.2024 at about 9:25 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Bellanduru Traffic Police Station, near Karmalaram Junction, Sarjapura Main road when the deceased Sri.Bijay Magar was crossing the road from Karmelaram road towards Siddapura Bus stand, at that time the accused/driver of the offending Eicher Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AN- 9257 came from Doddakannalli towards Kodathi and he drove the same in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endangering to human life and dashed against the deceased, as a result the said the deceased fall on the SCCH - 7 3 MVC No.34/2025 road and he has sustained grievous on stomach, legs and hands and other parts of the body and died at the spot.

Thereafter the accused run the offending vehicle without informing the alleged incident to the police station and without giving medical aid and he drove the said offending vehicle without possessing driving licence.

Thereafter,
brother of the deceased/Amith Magar lodged complaint before the Bellandur Traffic police station.

Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.107/2024 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 281 and 106(1) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023 R/w Section 134(a & b), 187, 3(1), 181, 5(1) and 180 of MV Act, and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial Magistrate and the superior Officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.
3.

It is contended that the Petitioner is the mother of the deceased Bijay Magar and as on the date of the alleged accident the said deceased was aged about 32 years and he was working in Hotel and earning income of Rs.25,000/- p.m.

The petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.30,00,000/-
under different head of loss of dependency, funeral and obsequies expenses, loss of filial love, loss of consortium and loss of estate etc.,
4.

It is contended that the accident is solely due to the rash or negligent driving of the accused/driver of the SCCH - 7 4 MVC No.34/2025 offending Eicher vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-AN-9257 and the respondent No.1 is the RC Owner and respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
5. In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 is placed exparte and Respondent No.2 has appeared through their counsel and filed their written statement.

In the written statement of respondent No.2, Respondent No.2 the Insurance Company by admitting that the offending vehicle was duly insured with it and the same is valid on the date of the accident and denying the petition averments in part and contended that the Petitioner has not furnished the particulars of the vehicle including the driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further it is denied having insured the vehicle involved in the accident.
The insurer liability is subjected to validity of the DL and other documents as per the law.
Further it is alleged that there is no compliance of provision under Section 134(C), 158 of M.V. Act.
Further it is alleged that the alleged accident is occurred due to negligence and fault of the deceased and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid D.L at the time of alleged accident.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtain the SCCH - 7 5 MVC No.34/2025 compensation Petitioner has constrained to file the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age, income and occupation of the deceased and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant and reserves the right u/s.170 of M.V.Act.
Hence sought for dismissal of the petition.
7. On the basis of above pleadings following Issues were framed.

:: I S S U E S ::
1) Whether the Petitioners proves that on 13.09.2024 at about 9-25 p.m., the deceased was a pedestrian on the extreme left side on Sarjapura Main road and after carefully crossing the road near Carmelaram Junction, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of offending Eicher Vehicle bearing registration No.KA- 01-AN-9257 drove the same in high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased and due to impact the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and he died ?
2) Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are legal heirs of deceased Bijay Magar?
3) Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

from whom?
 SCCH - 7 6 MVC No.34/2025  4) What order or award?

The Administrative Officer of the Insurance Company got examined as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.6 and closed their side.
9. I have heard the arguments of both side and perused the written arguments submitted by the respondent no.2.

REASONS 11. Issue No.1 : This petition is filed u/s.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for seeking compensation for the death of the deceased Sri.Bijay Magar S/o Late Yam B. Magar.

The petitioners' in the petition have contended that on 13.09.2024 at about 9:25 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Bellanduru Traffic Police Station, near Karmalaram Junction, Sarjapura Main road when the deceased Sri.Bijay Magar was crossing the road from Karmelaram road towards Siddapura Bus stand, at that time the accused/driver of the offending Eicher Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AN-9257 came from Doddakannalli towards Kodathi and he drove the same in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endangering to human life and dashed against the deceased, as a result the said the deceased fall on the road and he has sustained grievous on stomach, legs and hands and other parts of the body and died at the spot.
It is contended that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The Respondent No.2 admitted the alleged accident and its version is that, the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the deceased and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle,
however, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.
Further it is alleged that, driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid D.L, at the time of alleged accident.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtain the compensation Petitioners have constrained to filed the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age, income and occupation of the deceased and the petition is false and SCCH - 7 8 MVC No.34/2025 frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant and sought for dismissal of the petition.
13.
The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioners.

Hence, in order to prove their case,
the Petitioner herself examined as P.W.1 and she has reiterated the entire petition averments and contentions taken in the course of claim petition in her evidence before this Court and also produced as many as Exs.P.1 to Ex.P.19 documents.

In the cross-examination of PW-1 by the counsel for Respondent No.2 she has deposed that the deceased is her son.
Her husband was died prior to the alleged accident.
She is not doing any job.
She has agriculture lands in Nepal and her deceased son was working agriculture therein.
Due to her wedlock she has begotten four children and they are all major in age.
Her daughter was married and residing in her matrimonial house and her remaining children are doing job in agriculture and taking care of her.
The alleged accident was occurred on 13.09.2024 and she has was not an eye witness to the alleged accident.
Her another son Amith has lodged complaint.
She has not produced medical bills towards medical expenditure.
As the alleged accident occurred at night, they have lodged complaint on the next day of the alleged incident.
Prior to the alleged accident the deceased was working as Cook in the mobile canteen at Sarjapura.
She do not know owner of said mobile canteen.
She do not know whether her son will consume alcohol.

Further she has denied that, at the time of the alleged accident the deceased was consumed alcohol and negligently crossing the spot road and due to his fault the alleged accident was occurred and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle and the said vehicle is not involved in that incident.
Further she has denied that the deceased was not doing job in that mobile canteen hotel and not earning salary as alleged.
She do not know whether the deceased was consumed alcohol at the time SCCH - 7 10 MVC No.34/2025 of accident and in this regard report is given as per Ex.P- 10/FSL report.

Further she has denied that in order to get the compensation, in collusion with the police they have filed the false case against the driver of the offending vehicle and falsely implicated the offending vehicle and produced concocted and created documents and deposing falsely.
During the cross examination Pw.1 has consistently deposed on the lines of the petition and she has made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

15. In order to prove the version of Respondent No.2, the Respondent No.2 has examined its Administrative Officer as RW-1 and he has reiterated the entire version averments and contentions taken in the course of written statement in his evidence before this Court and also produced as many as Exs.R.1 and Ex.R.6 documents.
Therefore, there is no necessity to repeat those facts again.
I have gone through the documents produced by the RW-1.

Ex.R.1 is the copy of Authorization letter,
Ex.R.2 is the Insurance Policy, Ex.R.3 is the Letter dated 19.02.2025 issued to Respondent No.1,
Ex.R.4 is the Unserved RPAD postal envelop cover, Ex.R.4(a) is the Notice, Ex.R.5 is the Charge Sheet and Ex.R.6 is the FSL Report.

In the cross-examination of RW-1 by Petitioner's counsel he has deposed that at the time of the alleged accident the driver of the offending vehicle was not possessing valid driving licence to drive the offending SCCH - 7 11 MVC No.34/2025 vehicle, as such the police have filed Charge Sheet under MV Act against the driver and owner of the offending vehicle.
He has not produced documents to show that the accused was not possessing valid driving licence to drive the offending vehicle at the time of alleged accident.
After the alleged accident the officials of the Insurance Company have given Ex.R.3/Notice dated 19.02.2025 to owner of the offending vehicle.
After investigation the police have filed Charge Sheet against the accused person.
Further he has denied that in order to escape from their liability he has filed false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely.

On careful reading of Ex.P8/IMV report, it specifies that the Motor Vehicle Inspector has been clearly opined that, the said incident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the motor vehicles and further the said inspector noticed the damages to the offending vehicle that, no fresh visible damages noticed at the time of inspection.

17. On going through the Ex.P-5/Postmortem report it is seen that Doctor opined that cause of death is due to shock and haemorrhage as a result of multiple injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.

18. On going through the Ex.P-2/Complaint, it is seen that on 13.09.2024 at about 9:25 p.m., near Karmalaram SCCH - 7 12 MVC No.34/2025 Junction, Sarjapura Main road when the deceased Sri.Bijay Magar was crossing the road from Karmelaram road towards Siddapura Bus stand, at that time the accused/driver of the offending Eicher Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AN-9257 came from Doddakannalli towards Kodathi and he drove the same in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endangering to human life and dashed against the deceased, as a result the said the deceased fall on the road and he has sustained grievous on stomach, legs and hands and other parts of the body and died at the spot.
The alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.
19. Admittedly, the accused is the driver of the offending vehicle and further admitted that, Bijay Magar died due to alleged accident caused by the offending vehicle in question.

The counsel for Respondent No.2 claimed the said Accused to be innocent and further the counsel for Respondent No.2 contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to fault of the deceased and no fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent and the alleged accident occurred due to negligence and fault of the deceased, hence there is no negligence in the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Further the Respondent No.2 contended that the deceased was consumed alcohol and suddenly crossed SCCH - 7 13 MVC No.34/2025 the road negligently on taking note of the approaching offending vehicle and the driver of the offending vehicle cannot save accident, however, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.
The alleged accident occurred due to fault of the deceased and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.

On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, mahazar,
spot sketch, IMV Report, Inquest mahazar, Postmortem report and Charge Sheet and the evidence of PW-1 are specific to the effect that, the driver of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and she has supported the manner of occurrence in her evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/Complaint.
It seems that Pw.1 has clearly made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drew the offending vehicle in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed against deceased who was crossing the SCCH - 7 14 MVC No.34/2025 road, as a result the deceased Bijay Magar sustained grievous injuries and died Sharada Thapa vs Manjunatha K on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143806387/
6 due to alleged accident.

The evidence of Pw.1, Ex.P-1/FIR, Ex.P-2/Complaint, Ex.P.3/Spot Mahazar,
Ex.P.9/Spot sketch, Ex.P-8/IMV Report, Ex.P-5/Postmortem Report and Ex.P-6/Charge Sheet clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.
It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the deceased Bijay Magar sustained grievous injuries and died in the alleged incident.

Because,
for the above reasons collectively, it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash or negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries and cause of death of deceased Bijay Magar noted in the Ex.P.5/PM report would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 281 and 106(1) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023 R/w Sections 134 (a & b), 187, 3(1), 181, 5(1) and 180 of MV Act.

Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the death of the innocent man/Bijay Magar,
aforesaid, as he/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

SCCH - 7 15 MVC No.34/2025 20. Issue No.2 and 3:- The Learned counsel for the Petitioners has contended that the deceased was aged about 32 years and working in Hotel and earning income of Rs.25,000/- p.m.

Further the counsel contended that as per the Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram reported in 2018 ACJ 2782, the Petitioners being legal heirs of deceased, each of the Petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of love and affection consortium and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.
21.

sentences.text: Since the Petitioner has not established the income of the deceased, they are not entitled for compensation towards future prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.
On going through the Ex.P-14 and Ex.P.15/Adhar Cards it is seen that the Petitioner is the mother of the deceased.
Hence on the strength of Ex.P-14 and Ex.P.15 it is crystal clear that the Petitioner is the legal representative of the deceased.

23. The petitioners have contended that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 32 years and they relied on the Ex.P.15/Adhar Card of the deceased and wherein the date of birth of the deceased is shown as 14.09.1992 and this accident was took place on 13.09.2024.
Hence it is clear that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 31 years and 11 months.

Sharada Thapa vs Manjunatha K on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143806387/
7
Therefore, the age of the deceased is considered as 31 years at the time of accident.
24. It is not in dispute that the deceased died in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
In the instance case the petitioner claimed that deceased was working in Hotel and earning income of Rs.25,000/- p.m.
In this regard the Petitioner has produced Ex.P.16 Salary Certificate issued by the Proprietor of Uttar Karnataka Swadist Hotel.
On going through the same it is seen that the deceased was doing job as a Cook from 15.03.2023 to 04.06.2024 and earning salary of Rs.24,000/- p.m., therein.

In the instant case, the alleged accident was occurred on 13.09.2024, as such in SCCH - 7 17 MVC No.34/2025 pursuance of the Ex.P-16/Salary Certificate the deceased was not working in the said hotel as on the date of the alleged incident and the Petitioner has not examined the Proprietor of that hotel who issued the Ex.P-16/Salary certificate and he was not taken any pain to produce documents or to examine the owner of the mobile canteen hotel in which the deceased was doing job as a Cook as on the date of the alleged accident.

In this matter the alleged accident occurred on 13.09.2024 and the Petitioner has not produced any documents to show that the deceased was working as Cook in the mobile canteen hotel and earning income as alleged.
Under these circumstances Ex.P-16 document is not taken into consideration.
Hence in the absence of proof of income the notional income has to be assessed.

As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2024, the notional income of the deceased is taken at Rs.15,750/-.
25.

The Petitioner is considered as dependent of the deceased, in view of the law laid down by the constitution bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157 in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethy and other.

sentences.text:
Thus the 40% of the future prospects is to be added,
hence the monthly income comes to Rs.22,050/- (Rs.15,750/- + 40% = 6,300).

Since the deceased is the bachelor, it is appropriate to deduct SCCH - 7 18 MVC No.34/2025 50% towards personal and living expenses and remaining amount, i.e., Rs.11,025/- (Rs.22,050/- - Rs.11,025/-) has to be taken as his/deceased contribution to the family.
The deceased was aged about 31 years at the time of accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '16'.
Thus the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.21,16,800/- (Rs.11,025/- x 12 x 16) on account of loss of dependency.
26. In addition to that, the Petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of Loss of estate and compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of Funeral expenses.

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 2018 ACJ 2782 in the Case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram, Petitioner is the mother of the deceased is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of loss of filial consortium and also entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head of love and affection.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In view of the Pranay Sethi's case the Hon'ble Apex court in the year 2016 has stated that it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.40,000/-
towards consortium for dependents and this sum was to be increased by 10% every three years and consequently as of 2024, a sum of Rs.50,664/- is to be paid to the dependent towards head of loss of filial consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses caused by the loss of a deceased.

It cannot be SCCH - 7 19 MVC No.34/2025 in dispute that the loss of a deceased causes a devastating blow to the dependents and the degree of pain and agony would be at its speak and would linger forever it is for this reason an adequate sum is required to be awarded.
This sum can also be increased every year by adducing the record date of the inflation henceforth.

Accordingly now coming to the matter on Sharada Thapa vs Manjunatha K on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143806387/
8 hand, the Petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.19,000/- on account of Loss of estate and compensation of Rs.19,000/- on account of Funeral expenses.

The Petitioner is the mother of the deceased is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,664/- under the head of loss of consortium and also entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head of love and affection.

27. The details of compensation I propose to award are as under:
Sl. Compensation under different Amount in (Rs) No. heads 1 Loss of dependency 21,16,800-00 2 Funeral Expenses 19,000-00 3 Loss of Estate 19,000-00 4 Loss of filial consortium 50,664-00 5 Loss of love and affection 50,000-00
. The Petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.22,55,464/-.

The Respondent No.2/ Insurance Company admitted the alleged accident and alleged that the driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid and effective DL to drive the offending vehicle at the time of alleged accident and therefore after investigation the police have rightly filed Charge Sheet against the accused/driver and owner of the offending vehicle under Sections 281 and 106(1) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023 R/w Sections 134 (a & b), 187, 3(1), 181, 5(1) and 180 of MV Act and accordingly there is violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation.

30. In the instance case it is admitted fact that the driver of the offending vehicle has not possessing valid and effective driving licence to drive the offending vehicle at the time of the alleged accident and therefore there is clear violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, as such in view of breach of the policy condition the Petitioner prays to direct the Insurance Company to pay the compensation and recovered from the owner/ Respondent No.1 of the offending vehicle

and in this regard the Petitioner has relied in the decision reported in (2018) 3 SCC 208 in the case of Pappu and Others V/s Vinod Kumar Lamba and Another SCCH - 7 21 MVC No.34/2025 and (2018)
9 SCC 650 in the case of Shamanna and another V/s Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., and others.

3(1), 181, 5(1) and 180 of MV Act.

The counsel for Respondent No.2/Insurance Company contended that, in the instant case the alleged accident occurred on 13.09.2024 and the driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid and effective driving licence to drive the offending vehicle at the time of alleged accident, as such there is clear violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy and as per the new amendment of the provision of the M.V. Act which is effected from 01.04.2022 onwords if there is any violation of the insurance policy then the RC owner of the offending vehicle is liable to make the payment of compensation and it is not justified to direct the Insurance Company to pay compensation and then recover the said amount from the RC owner of the offending vehicle, thus in this matter there is breach of insurance policy condition and the concept of pay and recovery is unknown to the new amendment of the MV Act with effect from 01.04.2022 and such concept of pay and recovery applicable to prior to the effected date of the new amendment of the M.V.Act and therefore the counsel for Respondent No.2/Insurance Company contended that the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner and in this regard the counsel for Respondent No.2 has relied on the decision reported in 2022 SCC Online SC SCCH - 7 23 MVC No.34/2025 1888, SLP (C) NO.33638/2017 in the case of Balu Krishna Chavan V/w Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd., and Others.

sentences.text: Further the counsel fore Respondent No.2 contended that the deceased choose to cross the road at a high risk point instead of designated crossing, thereby voluntary exposing himself to danger.

sentences.text:
s Smt. Arti Devi and Others order dated 31.01.2025 of Hon'ble High Court of Alahabad, wherein the lordship held that:
SCCH - 7 25 MVC No.34/2025 "37.

....It is crystal clear that the object of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988, either before the amendment or thereafter, particularly covered by Chapter XI thereof, is to compensate victims of accidents in case of an insurance policy being in existence.

In view of the interpretation made, holding that omission of the proviso would exonerate the insurer of its liability to indemnify at the first instance would be too wild a proposition and would result in creating a situation where the insurer would be out of scene despite an insurance policy being there and the claimants would have to again fight for getting the amount of compensation through execution proceedings in one way or the other, searching the owner through the process of Court.

In such an event, the claimants would face further harassment and nobody knows that despite a money decree in the nature of an award being there in their favour, as to whether the claimants would ever be able to get the compensation realized through recovery proceedings directly from the owner.
Accordingly, the legislative intent becomes clear and there is nothing to support the insurer's arguments flowing from interpretation of Statute or Causus Omissus.
The contention advanced on behalf of insurer stands discarded.

Thus the lordship concluded that:
38.

The Court, therefore, holds that mere omission of proviso attached to sub- section (4) of Section 149 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 after its replacement by Section 150 of Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (32 of 2019), SCCH - 7 26 MVC No.34/2025 neither takes away the liability of the insurer to pay the claimants nor its right to recover the said amount from the owner.

The law to this effect remains intact and unaffected by Amendment Act, 2019 and, hence,
insurer shall continue to indemnify the owner's risk in relation to accidents taking place after 01.04.2022 and "PAY & RECOVER"
principle will still continue to govern the field advancing social object of the Statute protecting third party interest.

Principle of law laid down by the Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Swaran Singh and others, JT 2004 (1) SC 109 has not lost its significance and binding effect despite omission of proviso.

sentences.text: Held accordingly."

32. In the above case the principle of pay and recovery is explained in detail and the Hon'ble High Court held that the award passed against insured owner to be paid by the insurer and recovered from owner.

Hence in view of the position of law in the above recent decisions, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the award amount and Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle shall pay the compensation to the Petitioner and the Respondent No.2 Insurance Company shall recover the same from the Respondent No.1/owner of Sharada Thapa vs Manjunatha K on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143806387/

is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount within two months from the date of this order with liberty to recover the same in execution petition from respondent No.1 in the manner known to law.
